<!-- fathom:owned — generated by `fathom init --skills`; safe to delete this line to adopt the file as your own -->

## 1. Import an outbox

```sh
fathom findings import --store PATH --service S --subject ORG/REPO/COMPONENT \
  [--producer NAME] --file .reviewkit/outbox/projection.json [--dry-run] [--json]
```

- `--subject` must equal the event's own subject EXACTLY — check `.fathom/config.toml`'s `[findings] subject` (`docs/configuration.md`) before assuming a mismatch is a bug; it usually means the wrong subject was provisioned.
- `--producer`, when given, must match the events' own declared producer; a producer not in the catalog (`schema/semantic/producers.cue`) or not in this repo's `[findings] producers` allow-list is refused, never silently accepted at a lower tier.
- A `fathom`-origin producer is refused outright (`circular: native finding already exists as <claim_id>`) — authority never flows backwards from a review-kit journal to a native finding.
- When `.fathom/config.toml`'s `[findings] outbox` is set, this already runs automatically once per session (SessionStart/SubagentStart) — reach for this command by hand only to import an outbox NOT wired into config, or to see the receipt directly rather than the one-line brief summary.

## 2. Dry-run before you trust a new producer or subject

```sh
fathom findings import --store PATH --service S --subject ORG/REPO/COMPONENT \
  --file P --dry-run --json
```

Runs every validation (subject match, producer catalog, event ordering, digests) and returns the identical receipt shape WITHOUT writing anything — a store-state-equality guarantee, not a best-effort preview. Run this first the first time you point fathom at a new outbox.

## 3. Inspect what's open

```sh
fathom findings status     --store PATH --service S [--json]
fathom findings near       <symbol|file> --store PATH --service S [--hops 2] [--include-superseded] [--json]
fathom findings candidates --store PATH --service S [--min-sites 3] [--json]
```

- `status` reports the entry-condition progress plus, for the findings loop, `candidates` and `disagreements` counts — a `disagreement` is two producers reporting opposite outcomes (`fail`/`pass`) for the same rule and anchor, both served, never resolved for you.
- `near` finds findings within N call-graph hops of a symbol or file — the same precedent lookup used for native findings, working identically over imported ones.
- `candidates` derives RULE CANDIDATES from patterns recurring across `--min-sites` distinct sites, spanning native and external findings together — class, normalized shape, member citations, the producers that saw it, a drafted rule sentence, and the ADR-038 guard-check family that could enforce it. This is a report: fathom never writes a rule. A human decides whether to lift a candidate into `CLAUDE.md`/`.fathom/guard.cue`.

## 4. Refute or corroborate an EXTERNAL finding

```sh
fathom claim refute|corroborate --store PATH --service S --claim ID --note "..."
```

Works on an imported finding exactly as it does on a native one — the claim id from `findings status`/`findings near`. `refute` flips the claim's status with a durable note (suppression, never deletion); `corroborate` records provenance without touching status or tier. This is the ONLY way an imported finding's disposition changes inside fathom, and it is always a human verdict recorded against fathom's own claim — never a proxy for, or a write-back to, the review kit's own disposition (its own accept/dispute/tailor stays in ITS journal, not fathom's).

## 5. Read a receipt honestly

```json
{"schema_version": 1, "delivered": 3, "duplicate": 1, "stale": 0, "unclassified": 0,
 "rejected": [{"index": 4, "finding_id": "…", "reason": "conflicting-replay"}],
 "truncated": false, "cursors": [{"producer": "reviewkit.system-review", "latest_source_version": 7}],
 "dry_run": false}
```

- Exit code **1** on ANY `rejected` entry, even when the rest of the batch delivered — never report a receipt with rejections as a clean import.
- `stale` (an older `sourceVersion` than the cursor) and `duplicate` (identical replay) are both no-ops, but counted separately — report which one happened, they mean different things.
- `rejected` reasons you will see: `subject-mismatch`, `unknown-producer`, `circular` (fathom-origin), `conflicting-replay` (same version, different payload digest — re-derive from the review kit's own archive, never guess which payload is current). `docs/adoption/findings-loop.md`'s Troubleshooting section has the full list with fixes.
- `--dry-run` receipts carry `dry_run: true` and MUST show the same delivered/duplicate/stale/rejected counts a real run would — if a dry-run and the following real run disagree, that's a bug worth `fathom observe`-ing (see the `fathom-feedback` skill).

## 6. What fathom never does — say this out loud when asked

fathom never approves, disputes, tailors, or closes a review-kit finding on its own authority. It never translates a review-kit acceptance into a fathom `refute`, never re-derives or re-verifies an imported finding's truth, and never becomes the organizational record — retention, revocation, restore drills, and named operational owners stay the review kit's own. A finding served in the pre-edit hook is advisory: it names who observed what and when, `anchor_current` says whether the code has moved since, and nothing about serving it enforces anything. Only a HUMAN promoting a `findings candidates` output into `CLAUDE.md` or `.fathom/guard.cue` (and someone else's ADR-038 guard machinery actually compiling it) ever turns a finding into something that blocks an edit.

## 7. Reporting back

Summarize an import as: delivered/duplicate/stale/rejected counts, and — for any rejection — the reason and what it means (Troubleshooting above), never a bare "import failed." For a `candidates` report, name the class, the site count, and the drafted rule sentence; let the operator decide whether to promote it, never promote it yourself.
